english.title: Assault prisoner custody officer - direct managed prison
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) assaulted **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) a prisoner custody officer performing contracted out functions at a directly managed prison
english.legislation: Contrary to section 90(1) of the Criminal Justice Act 1991.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
assaulted
a prisoner custody officer
performing a contracted out function
at a directly managed prison

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 17(2) of the Firearms Act 1968 (additional penalty for possession of firearms when committing certain offences) applies to this offence - in those circumstances use offence wording H4354 for firearms, H4355 for shotguns and H4356 for airweapons .
(ii) A prisoner custody officer must be readily identifiable as such when acting in pursuance of prisoner escort arrangements - see section 90(4).
(iii) See the the charging standards relating to assaults.
(iv) This offence was added on 3.11.94 by section 100 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994.
(v) Section 40(3) of the Criminal Justice Act 1988 was amended by the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994 (paragraph 35 schedule 9) to include an offence under this section. This allows the offence to be added to an indictment if necessary.
(vi) See also associated offence wordings H4353 and H4406.

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.
(see note (iv) concerning mode of trial)

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
